items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: The gentleman that’s involved with that label, Progressive Records, Gus Statiras

ctx.x: “The Phantom.” And it re-surfaced after all this time.

Yeah. The gentleman that’s involved with that label, Progressive Records, Gus Statiras, who is a man with the thousands of records down in the lobby? He knew about that. He was around. There was a letter that came to me and it had my first name and then quotation marks The Phantom and then my last name, in care of the Half Note as a matter of fact, which was immediately put up like bulletin board style. And within a week, the jazz community in New York City in the 60s was very compact. Everybody knew everybody…

The nicknames seem to just hang on so, we have a book I’ve been reading and it has a whole chapter just about nicknames. They seem to stick really quick. Did you ever have one? You know I think, personally, that you were a comedian in another life.
